title: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents

object.carrier: Per-turn extracted memories stored in a local vector store (text-embedding-3-small embeddings, one namespace per cell), optionally carrying provenance/trust-weight metadata; defenses intercept at write (before storage) or read (retrieval into context)

safety_property.statement: The four defenses under study exist to preserve memory integrity (stop attacker-inserted text from becoming a stored memory that is later retrieved and treated as fact). This paper measures the benign-case price of that protection on entirely attack-free traffic: paired core-accuracy utility loss, defense-attributed token overhead, and false quarantine of legitimate memories (an availability cost). Write-time defenses show no resolvable utility cost; the read-time reranker shows a borderline accuracy cost and a clear false-quarantine cost, so the integrity protection trades against benign-memory availability and utility.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Benign utility delta (paired per-question core-accuracy change vs the undefended baseline; majority vote over three replicates, conversations weighted equally; stratified bootstrap 95% CI and exact McNemar and sign-flip tests; 255 core questions per replicate); token overhead ratio tau_d = defense-tagged tokens / baseline-tagged tokens across the 15 cells of each condition (Eq. 4); false quarantine rate FQR = pooled quarantines / pooled decisions (turns screened at write time, memories judged at read time; Eq. 5), where no content was planted so every quarantine is a false alarm by construction; companion rates: share of questions with at least one memory dropped and share of memories dropped at least once.

capabilities: Attacker inserts text into the conversation which becomes a memory that is later retrieved and treated as fact (the attack itself is outside the scope of this analysis; all measured traffic is benign)
assumptions: Evaluation corpus is benign by construction: no injected adversarial memory, so every item a defense quarantines is a false positive by definition
Memory backend, retrieval configuration, question set, answering model, and judge are held identical across conditions; only the defense varies, so any difference is attributable to the defense
The pipeline is non-deterministic even at temperature zero, so each condition is run three times and collapsed by majority vote before statistics
not_covered: Act-time interception is identified in the threat model but not evaluated; only write-time and read-time stages are measured
Attack success rates on adversarial traffic are not measured (no attacks are run)
Only one backbone (gemini-3.1-flash-lite) and one judge (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001); generalization to other models is untested

intervention.name: Comparison of four memory-poisoning defenses at two pipeline stages: write-time input sanitization, write-time provenance tagging, write-time LLM-based anomaly detection, read-time retrieval reranking, plus a stacked composition of all four
intervention.description: Sanitization lexically scans each candidate memory for injection patterns and discards or rewrites matches before storage (content layer, no model call); provenance tags record source and trust level, weighting memories from untrusted origins lower at storage and retrieval (provenance layer); anomaly detection passes each candidate to an LLM for consistency with the ongoing conversation and quarantines inconsistent candidates before commitment (content layer, model-based); the reranker re-evaluates retrieved candidates against the query and other retrieved memories on every question and quarantines poor matches from context (content layer at read time). The paper's central finding: benign-case utility cost tracks where the defense intercepts the pipeline (write vs read), not whether it uses an LLM.

controls.name: Stacked composition of all four defenses

results.claim: On entirely benign LoCoMo traffic, the read-time reranker lowers core accuracy by 4.4 points vs the undefended baseline (95% bootstrap CI [-9.0,-0.05]; McNemar p=0.064; 17 core questions changed right-to-wrong vs 7 in the opposite direction), with the sign consistent across all three replicates. (v2 note: the interval 'barely excludes zero'.)
results.metric: benign utility delta (paired core accuracy, pp)
results.setting: gemini-3.1-flash-lite backbone on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, 150-turn truncation, paired vs undefended baseline, no attack present
results.quote: The reranker reduced core accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [−9.0,−0.05][-9.0,-0.05]). The interval barely excludes zero, while McNemar’s test gives p=0.064p=0.064: 17 core questions changed from right to wrong, versus 7 that changed in the opposite direction.

denominator.how_counted: Paired core-accuracy change over 255 core questions per replicate (765 graded answers per condition; 5 conversations x 3 replicates), majority vote over replicates; 17 right-to-wrong vs 7 wrong-to-right discordant pairs drive the McNemar test (Sections 5.6, 7.1, 9)

results.claim: [replaced_by_different_metric in v2] The reranker quarantined 756 of 7,650 memory decisions (FQR 9.9%), vs 681 (8.9%) in the stacked condition; per cell the rate ranged 1.5%-19.3% (stacked 3.1%-22.7%), each dropped memory was dropped 2.2 times on average, 8.8% of stored memories were hidden at least once, and 45% of questions lost at least one retrieved memory (40% stacked). v1 reported 33.6% under a different counting: v1 FQR = quarantined items / adjudicated items per cell (averaged), v2 FQR = pooled quarantines / pooled memory decisions. The v1 'up to 106 false quarantines in a single conversation' now appears only as per-cell counts in Appendix B (Rerank conv-43: 106 quarantines, 19.3%).
results.metric: false quarantine rate (FQR) on benign traffic
results.setting: gemini-3.1-flash-lite backbone on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, benign corpus with no injected adversarial memory (every quarantine is a false positive by design)
results.quote: The reranker quarantined 756 of 7,650 memory decisions (FQR 9.9%), compared with 681 (8.9%) in the stacked condition. Per cell, the rate ranged from 1.5% to 19.3% (3.1% to 22.7% in the stacked condition).

denominator.how_counted: FQR = pooled quarantines / pooled decisions (memories judged at read time) over the 15 cells of the condition (Eq. 5, Section 5.5); v1 counted quarantined items over adjudicated items per cell and averaged, yielding 33.6% - different counting, not the same quantity

results.claim: Across entirely benign traffic, the three write-time defenses never fired (each screened 2,250 turns and quarantined none); their accuracy deltas are small and positive (+1.8 / +1.9 / +3.1 points for sanitize / provenance / anomaly) and every 95% CI includes zero, so no utility cost is resolvable at this scale. (v2 now reports the per-defense deltas that v1 summarized only as 'roughly ±4.5-point intervals'.)
results.value: write-time deltas +1.8/+1.9/+3.1 pp, each CI includes zero; FQR 0.0%
results.setting: gemini-3.1-flash-lite backbone on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, 150-turn truncation, paired vs undefended baseline, no attack present
results.quote: The three write-time defenses never fired on benign traffic. Each screened 2,250 turns and quarantined none. Because they did not change what the agent stored, their Δd\Delta_{d} reflects run-to-run noise. All three are small and positive, ranging from +1.8+1.8 to +3.1+3.1 points, and each interval includes zero.

denominator.how_counted: Each write-time defense screened 2,250 benign turns (5 conversations x 150 turns x 3 replicates) and made 2,250 verdicts with zero quarantines (Sections 7.1, 9)

results.claim: [interpretation revised in v2] Stacking all four defenses does not compound the cost: the stacked condition lost 3.1 points (95% CI [-7.4,+1.0]) with FQR 8.9%, close to the reranker alone. v1 suggested the write-time defenses 'may partly offset what the reranker discards'; v2 retracts that reading - the 1.3-point gap in Delta_d lies well inside the replicate spread, so the data do NOT show the defenses offsetting each other, and stacking did not compound only because the write-time stages never fired.
results.metric: benign utility delta (paired core accuracy, pp)
results.comparison: reranker alone -4.4 pp; gap 1.3 pp lies inside replicate spread (v2 wording)
results.setting: stacked configuration (sanitization, provenance, anomaly detection, reranking applied sequentially as wrappers), gemini-3.1-flash-lite on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, benign traffic
results.quote: Stacking did not compound the cost. The stacked condition lost 3.1 points (95% CI [−7.4,+1.0][-7.4,+1.0]) with FQR 8.9%, close to the reranker alone.

denominator.how_counted: Same paired core-accuracy protocol as the reranker row: 255 core questions per replicate, majority vote over 3 replicates (765 graded answers per condition); the stacked FQR 8.9% is 681 quarantines over 7,650 memory decisions (Sections 5.5, 7.4)

results.claim: The reranker's clearer cost is mechanical: 2.7% token overhead (tau_d), from one guard-model call per retrieved memory (2,550 calls per replicate); anomaly detection costs 1.2% (750 calls per replicate) and the stacked condition 4.1%, close to the sum 3.9%. (v1's 'up to 106 false quarantines in a single conversation' is carried in v2 only as per-cell counts in Appendix B and is recorded under the FQR entry.)
results.metric: token overhead ratio (tau) and max false quarantines per conversation
results.setting: rerank condition on benign LoCoMo traffic, per-purpose token accounting through a local proxy, 5 conversations x 3 replicates
results.quote: The reranker makes one call per retrieved memory, 2,550 per replicate, for 2.7%. The stacked condition pays both, 4.1%, close to their sum of 3.9%.

denominator.how_counted: tau_d = defense-tagged tokens / baseline-tagged tokens across the 15 cells of each condition (Eq. 4, Section 5.4); call counts 750 (anomaly, one per turn) and 2,550 (reranker, one per retrieved memory) per replicate

limitations.statement: Scale: intervals of 3.6-4.5 points mean costs of one or two points are undetectable; the write-time nulls do not establish zero cost, and the sign-flip test cannot go below p=0.0625 with five conversations.
limitations.quote: Interval half-widths remain between 3.6 and 4.5 points, making costs of one or two points hard to detect. Thus, the write-time nulls do not establish that the cost is zero.

limitations.statement: Single configuration: one backbone, memory framework, embedding model, and judge; a different backbone may change the reranker's FQR, and hosted models evolve so exact numbers may not reproduce.
limitations.quote: We test a single backbone, memory framework, embedding model, and judge. A different backbone may assess extracted memories differently and change the reranker’s FQR. Hosted models also evolve over time, so the exact numbers may not be reproducible.

limitations.statement: Benign traffic only: attack effectiveness is not measured, act-time defenses are untested, and stacked-filter interaction on triggering traffic is unknown.
limitations.quote: We measure costs only on benign traffic. We do not measure how effectively any defense stops attacks, test an act-time defense, or examine how stacked filters interact when they fire.

limitations.statement: Measurement provenance: a single annotator produced all hand labels and all 24 judge items come from one evaluation conversation (conv-26).
limitations.quote: A single annotator produced all hand labels. All 24 judge items come from conv-26, an evaluation conversation. Of the 89 abstention labels, we corrected 8 after the detector disagreed.

limitations.statement: The no-compounding finding is conditional: stacking did not compound cost because the write-time stages never fired; on traffic that triggers them, stacked filters may interact, and a benign corpus cannot test that.
limitations.quote: Stacking did not compound cost here because the write-time stages never fired. On traffic that triggers them, stacked filters may interact. A benign corpus cannot test that.

reproduction.code: Authors state all related code is provided with the paper (evidence alignment filter, judge prompts, abstention detector, complete per-cell outputs)
reproduction.data: LoCoMo dataset; 5 conversations truncated to 150 turns; 90 cells = 6 conditions x 5 conversations x 3 replicates
